commits.author: Tomas Bjerre
commits.message:
fix: inject @InjectWireMock fields without explicit SpringExtension (#213)

@ConfigureWireMock and @EnableWireMock only meta-annotated @ExtendWith
with WireMockSpringJunitExtension, which became a pure ParameterResolver
in #204. Field injection, resets and the default WireMock client now run
from a Spring TestExecutionListener, which only fires when SpringExtension
is registered - previously an implicit side effect of
SpringExtension.getApplicationContext() being called during field lookup.
Test classes without @SpringBootTest, @SpringJUnitConfig or an explicit
@ExtendWith(SpringExtension.class) got null @InjectWireMock fields.

Meta-annotate both annotations with an additional
@ExtendWith(SpringExtension.class); @ExtendWith is @Repeatable so this
stacks cleanly with whatever a test class already registers.

Fixes #212

Co-authored-by: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Tomas Bjerre
commits.message:
fix: only reset default WireMock client for tests that opt in (fixes #210) (#211)

* fix: only reset default WireMock client for tests that opt in (fixes #210)

4.4.0 moved resetting the static WireMock DSL client from
WireMockSpringJunitExtension into WireMockTestExecutionListener, but the
two have very different scope: the extension is registered by @ExtendWith
on @EnableWireMock/@ConfigureWireMock, whereas the listener is registered
in META-INF/spring.factories and so runs for every Spring test in any
project that merely has wiremock-spring-boot on its test classpath.

afterTestMethod called WireMock.configureFor(-1) unconditionally, which
for a test that never opted in clobbers whatever else configured the
static client - notably WireMock's own @WireMockTest extension, which
configures it once per test class. Every test method after the first then
addressed localhost with port -1, rendered as the URI default:

  org.apache.hc.client5.http.HttpHostConnectException:
  Connect to http://localhost:80 failed: Connection refused

beforeTestMethod and afterTestMethod now return early unless the test
class declares @EnableWireMock or @ConfigureWireMock, restoring the
pre-4.4.0 scope. prepareTestInstance stays ungated: it is already a
no-op without @InjectWireMock fields, and gating it would turn a missing
@EnableWireMock from a clear IllegalStateException into a silently unset
field.

Adds usecases.CoreWireMockTestAnnotationTest, a @SpringBootTest using
@WireMockTest that stubs with the static DSL in two ordered test
methods. It fails on main with exactly the reported error and passes
with this change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test: add the reproduction reported in #210

Adds corewiremock.GetNumberAdapterTest, the scenario from the issue
itself: a @SpringBootTest whose service bean talks to a statically
configured port via RestClient, stubbed with the static WireMock DSL
through WireMock's own @WireMockTest. Without the preceding fix its
second test method fails with the reported error,

  org.apache.hc.client5.http.HttpHostConnectException:
  Connect to http://localhost:80 failed: Connection refused

This needs RestClient.Builder to be auto-configured, which in Spring
Boot 4 lives in spring-boot-starter-restclient rather than
spring-boot-starter-web, so that starter is added as a test dependency.

The adapter bean and its @SpringBootApplication live in their own
top-level package, so that usecases.App's component scan over the
"usecases" package does not sweep the bean into every other test's
application context - the same reason nodirtycontext has its own app.
CoreWireMockTestAnnotationTest moves there too, keeping both tests for
this regression together: that one covers the same defect with a
dynamic port and no service bean.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test: stub #210's reproduction with rest-assured, drop the RestClient scaffolding

The RestClient in the issue was incidental: the call that fails is
stubFor, WireMock's own admin call over the static DSL client, not the
application's request. So the service bean added nothing to the
reproduction, and everything propping it up went with it - the
@SpringBootApplication that existed only to keep that @Service out of
usecases.App's component scan, and the spring-boot-starter-restclient
test dependency that RestClient.Builder injection needed.

The test is now a single class in usecases that stubs and asserts with
rest-assured, like the rest of the suite, keeping the issue's fixed
port and its status404/statusOk methods. It still fails without the
preceding fix with the reported error:

  org.apache.hc.client5.http.HttpHostConnectException:
  Connect to http://localhost:80 failed: Connection refused

Also drops the duplicate rest-assured testImplementation line.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Tomas Bjerre
commits.message:
refactor: split WireMockServerCreator.createWireMockServer into named steps

The method mixed ~9 distinct concerns inline - resolving ports and TLS,
mappings/extensions/templating/customizers, starting the server,
registering shutdown hooks, publishing 4 groups of Spring properties in
near-identical blocks, and Spring bean registration - in one ~120 line
method. Split into buildServerOptions, registerShutdownHooks and
publishServerProperties (plus small publishProperties/publishProperty
helpers replacing the 4 repeated blocks), so the top-level method now
reads as a short sequence of named steps.

Derives httpEnabled/httpsEnabled from the started WireMockServer
(isHttpEnabled()/isHttpsEnabled()) instead of threading local booleans
computed earlier in the method through to the property-publishing
step - same values, one less thing to pass around.

Log message text is unchanged (verified no test asserts on it).
Behavior and ordering are otherwise identical.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Tomas Bjerre
commits.message:
refactor: extract shared resolveConfigureWireMocks helper

WireMockTestExecutionListener.resetWireMockServersIfConfigured had
two near-identical blocks - one iterating EnableWireMock-derived
ConfigureWireMock entries, one iterating standalone ones - that both
did the same filter(resetWireMockServer).map(lookup).forEach(resetAll)
afterward. The "flatten EnableWireMock + standalone ConfigureWireMock
entries for a class" step itself was also duplicated with
WireMockContextCustomizerFactory.parseDefinitions.

Extracts that resolution into
WireMockContextCustomizerFactory.resolveConfigureWireMocks(Class<?>),
and uses it in resetWireMockServersIfConfigured, which shrinks from
two loops to one. parseDefinitions is left as-is since it has
different semantics (validates via add(), skips by name via
addIfAbsent()) that don't map cleanly onto a flat resolve.

configureWireMockForDefaultInstance also duplicates this resolution
step, but its "pick the one default candidate" branching has enough
particular behavior (e.g. a multi-entry EnableWireMock group still
picks index 0 with just a log warning, while multiple groups aborts
entirely) that folding it into this helper deserves its own pass with
dedicated test coverage rather than being bundled here.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Merge pull request #207 from wiremock/perf/cache-annotation-scans

perf: cache reflection-based annotation and field scans per test class

commits.author: Tomas Bjerre
commits.message:
perf: cache reflection-based annotation and field scans per test class

WireMockContextCustomizerFactory.getEnableWireMockAnnotations,
getStandaloneConfigureWireMockAnnotations, and
WireMockTestExecutionListener's @InjectWireMock field scan all
re-walk a class's annotations/fields via reflection on every call.
Since WireMockTestExecutionListener now drives this on every test
method (not just once per test class), and resetWireMockServersIfConfigured
and configureWireMockForDefaultInstance each independently re-scan
the same class within a single beforeTestMethod call, the same
reflection work was being redone on every single test.

A test class's own annotations and fields can't change during a JVM
run, so memoize each per Class<?> in a ConcurrentHashMap. Repeated
calls for the same class become an O(1) lookup instead of a fresh
reflective scan.

The recursive enclosing/superclass lookup inside each scan had to be
changed to call the uncached scan method rather than the cached entry
point - ConcurrentHashMap.computeIfAbsent forbids its mapping
function from making another computeIfAbsent call on the same map
("Recursive update"), which EnableWireMockOnSuperClassAndSubClassTest
caught as a flaky IllegalStateException depending on cache-population
order across the suite.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

perf: log Store context resolution at debug instead of info

commits.author: Tomas Bjerre
commits.message:
perf: log Store context resolution at debug instead of info

Store.resolve(ApplicationContext) is now called several times per
test method (once per @InjectWireMock field, once per server reset,
once for the default-instance lookup) since
WireMockTestExecutionListener drives this on every test rather than
once per test class. Logging it at INFO added synchronous log I/O on
every one of those calls, for a message that never varies within a
run and isn't actionable. DEBUG is more appropriate for this level of
per-call, high-frequency internal bookkeeping.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
Merge pull request #205 from wiremock/test/189-static-port-no-dirty-context-coverage

test: verify staticPortDirtySpringContext=false actually prevents dirtying

commits.author: Tomas Bjerre
commits.message:
test: verify staticPortDirtySpringContext=false actually prevents dirtying (refs #189)

The existing StaticPortNoDirtyContextTest only asserted that the
configured port was applied - that assertion would pass even if
staticPortDirtySpringContext did nothing at all, so it gave no
coverage for the actual regression #189 reported (a shared BaseIT
losing Spring's test context cache reuse).

Replaces it with a test that drives two independent
TestContextManager instances for the same configuration directly and
asserts they resolve to the exact same ApplicationContext, with a
context-creation counter bean as a second, independent signal. This
avoids relying on JUnit Jupiter's cross-class execution order (which
is not guaranteed) to prove context reuse across "two test classes".

The counter bean lives in its own top-level package (nodirtycontext)
rather than under an existing one, since @SpringBootApplication's
default component scan is based on package, not source file, and an
existing @ComponentScan elsewhere in the suite (usecases.App, and
even the nested AppConfiguration classes under the flat `test`
package) would otherwise silently sweep it up and inflate the count
from unrelated tests - this was verified against the full suite, not
just this test in isolation.

Verified the new test fails as expected when
staticPortDirtySpringContext is flipped back to true, both in
isolation and as part of the full suite.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Tomas Bjerre
commits.message:
feat: support test engines other than JUnit Jupiter (refs #198)

Moves per-test WireMock behavior - resetting servers, configuring the
default WireMock client, and injecting @InjectWireMock fields - from
WireMockSpringJunitExtension (a JUnit Jupiter-only extension) into
WireMockTestExecutionListener, a Spring TestExecutionListener already
auto-registered via spring.factories.

TestExecutionListener is invoked by Spring's TestContextManager
regardless of which test engine drives it, so this also makes
resetWireMockServer and the default WireMock client work under
Cucumber (via cucumber-spring), TestNG and JUnit 4, not just JUnit
Jupiter. Annotation discovery reuses
WireMockContextCustomizerFactory's existing class-based scanning
(which already walks enclosing/superclasses for @Nested support), so
@Nested JUnit Jupiter tests are unaffected.

@InjectWireMock on a constructor/method *parameter* remains JUnit
Jupiter-only (no Spring TestContext equivalent), so
WireMockSpringJunitExtension now only implements ParameterResolver.

Field injection of @InjectWireMock does not reach Cucumber
glue/step-definition classes, since those are managed as regular
Spring beans by cucumber-spring rather than as TestContextManager
test instances - they still need @Autowired/@Qualifier with
registerSpringBean=true, as before. Updated the usecases/cucumber
example to drop its manual resetAll() call and use the static
WireMock DSL client, proving both now work automatically.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Fausto Moya
commits.message:
fix: stop WireMock servers when context closes during AOT processing (#200)

During Spring test AOT processing (SpringBootTestAotProcessor), the test
application context is loaded and closed outside the JUnit lifecycle.
The ContextClosedEvent is never delivered in that case (the event
multicaster is not initialized by refreshForAotProcessing), so the
WireMock servers were never stopped and their non-daemon Jetty threads
kept the AOT processing JVM alive forever, hanging processTestAot.

Singletons are still destroyed when that context is closed, so each
started server is now also registered as a disposable bean. The existing
ContextClosedEvent listener is kept, and both paths are guarded against
double-stop.

Fixes #199

Co-authored-by: moyis <fausto@moyis.dev>
